title: Kaya Toast with Soft Boiled Eggs

tools.name: Heatproof mixing bowl
tools.note: Set it over the saucepan so the bowl sits above the water without touching it.

tools.name: Saucepan
tools.note: A small saucepan works best for both the caramel and warming the coconut milk.

tools.name: Jar or bowl
tools.note: Use a clean one; either a jar or a bowl will work for cooling the kaya.

tools.name: Pot
tools.note: Use a small pot with a lid for cooking the eggs.

tools.name: Bowl
tools.note: Four small bowls are used for serving the eggs, so the size is small and the count is four.

tools.name: Kitchen timer
tools.note: A phone or any clock with a second hand can stand in for it.

steps.title: Mix kaya custard base
points: Take the 4 eggs for serving out of the fridge so they lose their chill.
Crack the 3 kaya eggs into the heatproof bowl, add the 1/2 cup sugar and the salt, and whisk until the sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Pour the mixture through the fine-mesh strainer into a measuring cup, rinse the bowl, and pour the strained mixture back in.
Cut the cold butter into thin slices and keep it in the fridge.

steps.title: Combine custard over simmering water
points: Whisk the egg mixture constantly while you pour the warm caramel coconut milk into it in a thin stream.
Fill the medium saucepan with about 2 inches of water and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat.
Set the bowl on top, making sure the bottom does not touch the water.

steps.title: Cook the kaya
points: Cook the kaya, stirring and scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl with the spatula without stopping, for 30 to 40 minutes.
It will go from thin to a thick custard that coats the spatula heavily and holds a line when you draw a finger through it.
Keep the water at a bare simmer the whole time.
Scrape the kaya into the jar and let it cool for at least 30 minutes; it thickens further as it cools.

steps.title: Heat water and set the eggs
points: When the kaya has cooled, fill the small pot with enough water to cover the eggs by 1 inch and bring it to a full boil over high heat.
Turn off the heat, lower the 4 eggs in with the slotted spoon, cover the pot, and set the timer for 7 minutes.

steps.title: Assemble kaya toast sandwiches
points: While the eggs sit, toast the bread until deep golden and crisp, then trim off the crusts if you like.
Spread kaya thickly on 4 slices, lay the cold butter slices over the kaya, and close each sandwich with a second slice of toast.

steps.title: Lift and season the eggs
points: When the timer goes, lift the eggs out with the slotted spoon.
Crack each egg into a small bowl; the whites will be just set and the yolks runny.
Add 1/2 teaspoon soy sauce and a pinch of white pepper to each bowl, stir gently, and serve with the toast for dipping.

troubleshooting.problem: The kaya turns grainy or has bits of cooked egg in it
troubleshooting.solution: Keep the water at a bare simmer and stir without stopping. If it has already happened, push the warm kaya through the fine-mesh strainer.

troubleshooting.problem: The kaya is still runny after 40 minutes
troubleshooting.solution: Turn the heat up slightly so the water simmers steadily, and keep stirring until it holds a line.

troubleshooting.problem: The egg whites are watery and clear
troubleshooting.solution: Let them sit out longer next time, or leave them covered in the hot water for 1 to 2 more minutes.

troubleshooting.problem: The butter melts into the toast
troubleshooting.solution: The toast was too hot or the butter was too warm. Keep the butter in the fridge until you assemble, and let the toast sit for 1 minute before spreading.
